shortDefinition: A system design where human review and approval is required at critical steps in an AI workflow.
fullDefinition: Human-in-the-loop (HITL) refers to AI workflows that are designed to include human checkpoints at critical decision points rather than operating fully autonomously. This is a safety design principle: let AI handle high-volume, low-stakes steps autonomously, but require human approval before consequential actions. HITL reduces error risk and maintains accountability in AI-assisted processes.
